name: Atlas Roofing Co. v. Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission
summary: The Supreme Court upheld Congress's authority to allow an administrative agency to impose monetary penalties for OSHA violations without a jury trial, reasoning that 'public rights' created by statute may be adjudicated outside Article III courts.
significance: Held that Congress may assign adjudication of certain statutory penalties to administrative agencies without a jury trial, which the government argues supports its authority to adjudicate H-2A monetary remedies in-house.
